title: Common Errors
markdown:
## Messages

| Message or symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReferenceError: x is not defined` | A typo in a name, or a variable used outside its block | Check the spelling; declare it where it is used | 2.04 |
| `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'x' before initialization` | A `let` / `const` (or a `const` function) used above its declaration | Move the declaration up, or use a function declaration | 2.01 |
| `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` | Reading a property of something that is `undefined`: a missing argument, a wrong key, a `find` with no match | Check where the value comes from; use `?.` when it may really be missing | 1.03 |
| `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` | `document.querySelector` matched nothing | Check the selector and that the element exists when the script runs | 6.01 |
| `TypeError: x is not a function` | Calling a value that is not a function: a typo in a method name, a missing `()` elsewhere, a wrong import | Log `typeof x`; check imports and names | 2.01 |
| `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.` | Reassigning a `const` | Use `let` if it really must change | 1.02 |
| `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` inside a method used as a callback | `this` was lost: `setTimeout(obj.method)`, `arr.map(obj.method)` | `() => obj.method()` or `obj.method.bind(obj)` | 3.02 |
| `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'` in `JSON.parse` | The text is HTML (often a 404 page), not JSON | Check `response.ok` and the URL before parsing | 4.04 |
| `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` | Parsing an empty string | Check the text is non-empty; handle missing data | 2.05 |
| `SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions` | `await` in a normal function | Mark the function `async`, or use a module's top level | 4.03 |
| `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` | Node treats the file as CommonJS | `"type": "module"` in `package.json`, or a `.mjs` file | 3.05 |
| `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` | Recursion without a base case, or a getter or setter that calls itself | Add the base case; store the value in a different (`#private`) field | 3.01 |
| `Uncaught (in promise)` / unhandled rejection | A rejected promise nobody handled | `await` it inside `try`, or add `.catch` | 4.02 |
| `Failed to fetch` / CORS error | The server does not allow your page's origin, or the network is down | Fix the server's CORS headers, or call through your own backend | 4.04 |

## Wrong results without an error

| Symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"2" + 3` gives `"23"` | `+` joins when either side is a string; form and prompt values are strings | Convert first: `Number(text)` | 1.03 |
| `0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3` | Floating-point rounding | Compare with a tolerance, or work in whole cents | 1.02 |
| `[10, 9, 1].sort()` gives `[1, 10, 9]` | `sort` compares as strings by default | `sort((a, b) => a - b)` | 2.02 |
| A setting of `0` or `""` is replaced by the default | `value \|\| fallback` treats them as missing | `value ?? fallback` | 1.03 |
| A copied object changes when the original does | Spread and `Object.assign` copy one level only | Copy nested objects too, or `structuredClone` | 2.03 |
| The caller's array was changed | `sort`, `reverse`, `splice` change the array in place | Work on a copy: `[...arr].sort()`, `toSorted()` | 2.02 |
| An async function returns `Promise {<pending>}` | Its result was not awaited | `await f()` or `f().then(...)` | 4.03 |
| `forEach(async ...)` finishes before the work does | `forEach` ignores the returned promises | `for...of` with `await`, or `Promise.all(arr.map(...))` | 4.03 |
| A 404 response is treated as success | `fetch` only rejects on network failure | Check `response.ok` | 4.04 |
| Every callback from a loop sees the last value | `var` shares one variable across the loop | Use `let` | 2.04 |
| `typeof null === "object"` | A historical quirk | Check `x === null` first | 1.02 |
| `NaN === NaN` is false | `NaN` is never equal to anything | `Number.isNaN(x)` | 1.03 |
| A spread of a Map into JSON gives `{}` | `JSON.stringify` ignores Map and Set contents | `Object.fromEntries(map)`, `[...set]` | 2.05 |
| User text shows up as HTML or runs a script | `innerHTML` with unescaped text | `textContent`, or escape the text | 6.01 |
| A form reloads the page | The submit's default action was not cancelled | `event.preventDefault()` | 6.02 |
| A number from `FormData` or `localStorage` compares wrongly | Both give strings | `Number(value)` | 6.03 |

## TypeScript

| Message | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'number'` | The wrong type passed | Convert the value, or fix the parameter type if it is wrong | 5.01 |
| `TS18048: 'x' is possibly 'undefined'` | A value that may be missing is used directly | Check it first (`if (x === undefined) ...`), or give a default with `??` | 5.01 |
| `TS2339: Property 'radius' does not exist on type 'Shape'` | Using a variant's property without narrowing | Check `shape.kind` first | 5.03 |
| `TS2322: Type '"north"' is not assignable to type 'Direction'` | A value outside a literal union | Use one of the allowed values, or extend the type | 5.03 |
| `TS7006: Parameter 'x' implicitly has an 'any' type` | A parameter without a type in strict mode | Annotate it | 5.01 |
| `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties` | A typo or extra property in an object literal | Fix the name, or add the property to the type | 5.02 |
| `TS2322: Type 'X' is not assignable to type 'never'` | A switch over a union is missing a case | Handle the new variant | 5.03 |
| `TS2540: Cannot assign to 'id' because it is a read-only property` | Changing a `readonly` property | Create a new object instead | 5.02 |
